name: John
overview: John, also called Mark, is a male figure mentioned in Acts 12:12 as a companion of Barnabas and Saul. He is likely the author of the book of Mark. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as a close associate of key early Christian leaders highlights his importance in the early church.
namesAndTitles: The name John means 'y-h-v-h is gracious,' reflecting a recognition of God's grace, while the name Mark is also used for this individual without a given meaning. Both are proper names recorded in Acts 12:12.
familyAndRelationships: John is identified as the son of Mary, inferred from Acts 12:12. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him apart from those noted in his unique attributes.
scriptureSignificance: John is significant as a close companion of Barnabas and Saul during the formative years of the early church, indicating his active participation in the spread of the gospel. His likely authorship of the book of Mark contributes to the New Testament witness by providing a detailed account of Jesus' life and ministry. This connection underscores his role in preserving and communicating the message of Christ.
